A beat starts with the first window that opens after its server windows are live on prod, the backend release instant read in UTC, not when its client PRs merged. Collect & Win runs Mon-Tue, Wed-Thu and Fri-Sun, each opening 00:00 UTC, so a window the release instant pre-empts does not count. A beat that is only waiting on that release starts late, it is not held.

sources.quote: Hold a beat only when players provably cannot enter, score or claim on prod even after a restart. An established failure holds it; an unverified build or platform is a still-to-do, not a hold. Wrong counters, a reset that needs a restart, cosmetic, VFX and performance gaps and analytics gaps do not hold a beat
A one-off may take a recurring beat slot only with Product latest dated approval, and if he takes that back his later word is the one that counts.

For each beat, what still has to land before it runs for bought users (prod deploy, config, player-facing art an owner has flagged) and who owns it. Not what already shipped, not analytics, not polish nobody flagged.
A push goes out only if its row is Ready and LIVE and its English copy names the game only as Zombie Match 3D and events only by their ZM3D names. Anything else is held, with what is missing.
Every config a beat needs lands before its lock, read in server time (UTC). A committed date that misses the lock moves earlier and its owner is told.
Every ZM3D beat a player can see in those weeks: an event window, a reset or a start push. Not only the events everyone lists. Boss Arena is off this calendar until the pivot call.
For the quest rollover and the daily gift (the Login Calendar row on the push sheet) put down whether the beat is in and whether its push is ready, not its window dates.
